dns.title: DNS - Domain Name System
dns.content:
֎ DNS helps UE/gNB/5GC discover IP address and resolve FQDN of network functions or DN (Data Network).
          • gNB ----Where is AMF?----> DNS
          • AMF ----Where is SMF?----> DNS
          • SMF ----Where is UPF?----> DNS
֎ During PDU Session establishment, SMF use DNS to resolve :
          • Fully Qualified Domain name (FQDN) of UPF.
          • FQDN of DN/ Internet gateway.
          • External services if a UE requests a domain.

              <--------------------Inside the core---------------><-------Outside the core----->
֎           UE --> gNB --> AMF -------> DNS <------- SMF : DNS ---------------------> UE
                                • Initial Reg. of UE to the AMF →
                                • AMF resolves SMF FQDN →
                                • SMF resolves UPF FQDN →
                                • DNS connect UE to the server

֎ Without DNS :
          • Network Function can't find each other.
          • UE can't reach website.
          • PDU session would fail at UPF selection range.

mdns.title: mDNS - Multicast DNS
mdns.content:
֎ Multicast DNS over UDP (Port : 5353) (Multicast Ip : 224.0.0.251).
֎ Local n/w service discovery portal.
֎ It allows devices in the same LAN to discover each other without a DNS server.
          • Example devices - Chorecast, Smart T.Vs, IoT Devices, Printers, cameras
     Normal DNS : asks a DNS server
     mDNS : shoutout in LAN => "Who has this name?". Devices reply to everyone
֎ mDNS is not a part of 5G protocol or PDU session establishment.

          UE ------> mDNS multicast ------> Local devices in same subnet (multicast)

֎ mDNS is useful to test multicast support.
֎ In 5G private n/w, mDNS is often used for -
          • local device discovery
          • edge computing service announcements
          • zero configuration networking
֎ If UPF doesnot allow multicast then mDNS fails.

icmp.title: ICMP - Internet Control Message Protocol
icmp.content:
֎ ICMP is used for network reachability testing & error reporting.
֎ Example ping : ICMP echo req/ echo reply.                        
          • Tells if a server , UPF or any other IP is reachable.
          • Latency check.
֎ ICMP works on IP layer therefore no port needed.
֎ ICMP is not used inside 5GC-CP.
֎ It is just used to check reachability & routing for UPF, SMF, DN, AMF etc.
֎ ICMP versions : ICMP & ICMPv6

                      ---------------Send ICMP echo req--------------->
                      UE                                 UPF                               DN
                      <----------ICMP echo reply comes back----------

ICMP confirms :
          • ICMP helps verify end-to-end IP connectivity.
          • UPF forwarding rules are correct.
          • Internet breakout ok.
          • NAT/Firewall is not blocking UE traffic.

ntp.title: NTP - Network Time Protocol
ntp.content:
֎ NTP is used to synchronise time across all devices and servers in a network.
          • Ensures accurate system clock.
          • Correct logging, security check & protocol timing.
֎ Port: UDP 123
֎ Why Time is Important in 5G:
          • Required for secure authentication (5G-AKA)
          • Needed for charging and billing accuracy      
          • Critical for URLLC timing precision                 
          • Keeps network functions synchronized           
֎ 5G prefers PTP (IEEE1588) for radio timing as it provides very accurate sync over ethernet but NTP is heavily used for core n/w timing.
֎ Large offset in the Delay & offset Field implies out of sync.
֎ NTP Versions:
          • NTPv4 (most common) & SNTP (Simple NTP – lightweight version)
֎ Time Accuracy:
          • Millisecond level over internet                  
          • Microsecond level in controlled networks

quic.title: QUIC - Quick UDP Internet Connections
quic.content:
֎ It is a modern transport protocol built on the top of the UDP, designed by google & later adopted as an IETF standard.
֎ Transport: UDP (Port 443)
֎ Used in HTTP/3
֎ Used By: Youtube, google services, facebook, Instagram, Netflix, Chrome, firefox, etc.
֎ QUIC replaces -
          • TCP handshake
          • TLS handshake
          • Some HTTP functions
֎ QUIC gives - faster connection setup, better performance in mobile networks, stream multiplexing, Built-in encryption
֎ QUIC integrates transport + TLS + multiplexing similar to HTTP/2 features.
It is a combination of one fast protocol over UDP.
֎ Purpose:
          • Fast and secure internet communication
          • Reduces connection setup time
          • Built-in encryption (TLS 1.3) : Everything QUIC sends is encrypted, even packet number.
          • QUIC can't be decoded unless you have TLS key.
֎ Main Features:
          • Lower latency compared to TCP+TLS
          • Handles mobility better ie. improved mobile performance
          • 0-RTT connection setup ie. quick handshakes
          • No head-of-line blocking
          • Multiplexed streams
          • Better throughput over radio (less sensitive to packet loss).
֎ In 5G:
          • QUIC is not a part of 5G core signaling but heavily used in user-plane traffic.
          • QUIC is not used for registration/NAS/NGAP/SMF or UPF communication/PFCP/GTP-U.
          • Faster web browsing over high-speed 5G
          • Better performance in mobility scenarios
          • After PDU session establishment, QUIC traffics is extreamly common as most APPs running on UE now use QUIC.
֎ Encapsulation in 5G:
           UE ---> establishes PDU session ---> UE opens YT : UE-->gNB-->UPF-->DN(Traffic)
                     • UPF sees UDP/443 port packets (QUIC Packets)
                     • YT responds with QUIC encrypted video streams.

tls.title: SSL/TLS - Secure Transport Layer
tls.content:
֎ Full Form:
          • SSL: Secure Sockets Layer (old version)
          • TLS: Transport Layer Security (modern version TLS 1.3)
֎ Layer: Operates between transport and application layers
֎ Works With: TCP
֎ Purpose:
          • Provides encryption + authentication for secures client–server communication
          • It also ensures data integrity
          • TLS encrypts all data after handshake
֎ Used In:
          • HTTPS websites, Banking applications, Secure APIs, Email security
֎ TLS 1.3 Handshake:
          • Client Hello
          • Server Hello
          • Encrypted Handshake
          • Encrypted Application Data
֎ In 5G Core:
          • SSL is not used inside 5G core signaling.
          • Core uses HTTP/2 + TLSv1.3 for SBI (NF ↔ NF communication)
          • Protects control plane service-based interfaces
          • Not used for NAS or RRC signaling, ie. TLS is not a part of PDU session signaling.
          • TLS traffic usually appears after IP connectivity (PDU session) is established.
֎ Inside Core : TLS provides cybersecurity in SBI.
֎ In User Plane Traffic : Apps use HTTPS (TLS 1.3) for encrypted data streaming.
֎ Encapsulation:
          • GTP-U tunnels TLS traffic between gNB & UPF.
          • TLS over TCP over IP → GTP-U → 5G Tunnel
֎ Important:
          • Without TLS → Data travels in plain text
          • With TLS → Data is encrypted

tcp.title: TCP - Transmission Control Protocol
tcp.content:
֎ Layer: Transport Layer (Layer 4)
֎ It is the most common transport layer protocol befor QUIC.
֎ Main Features:
          • Reliable delivery
          • Ordered packets
          • Retransmission of lost packets
          • Flow control (window size)
          • Congestion control
          • Connection-oriented (3-way handshake)
֎ 3-Way Handshake:
          • SYN (Client → Server)
          • SYN-ACK (Server → Client)
          • ACK (Client → Server)
Connection Established. After this TLS may start.
֎ Connection Termination:
          • FIN
          • RST (Reset if needed)
          • Retransmission
֎ Used In:
          • HTTPS (TLS over TCP)
          • API calls
          • File downloads
          • Web browsing (HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2)
֎ In 5G:
          • Not used in RAN control signaling (Control plane uses SCTP between gNB<-->AMF)
          • Used inside core : HTTP/2 over TLS over TCP (SBI communication)
          • All SBI messages ultimately rides over TCP (Inside Core) ie. SBI uses HTTP/2 over TLS over TCP.           • Most apps use HTTP over TCP (UPF after PDU session setup)
֎ Encapsulation in 5G User Plane:
          UE TCP Packets → IP → GTP-U Tunnel → UPF → Data Network

udp.title: UDP - User Datagram Protocol
udp.content:
֎ Layer: Transport Layer (Layer 4)
֎ Connectionless transport protocol.
֎ Faster than TCP (no handshake, no retransmission control).
֎ Main Features:
          • No connection setup
          • No guaranteed delivery
          • No packet ordering
          • Low latency
          • Small header (8 bytes)
֎ No Handshake:
          • Data sent directly
          • No SYN / ACK process
֎ Used In:
          • DNS
          • NTP
          • QUIC
          • RTP (Voice / Video)
          • Online gaming
֎ In 5G:
          • Used for PFCP (SMF ↔ UPF over N4)
          • Used for DNS and QUIC traffic from UE
          • Used for RTP in IMS (VoNR media)
          • Preferred for low-latency applications
֎ Encapsulation in 5G User Plane:
          UE UDP Packets → IP → GTP-U Tunnel → UPF → Data Network

sip.title: SIP - Session Initiation Protocol
sip.content:
֎ Layer: Application Layer (Layer 7)
֎ SIP is a signaling protocol (control plane of IMS) used to set up, modify and tear down voice/video calls over IP.
  SIP signaling is carried over the user plane via IMS PDU session, not 5G-CP signaling.
֎ Purpose:
          • Call setup
          • Call modification
          • Call termination
          • User registration in IMS
֎ Important:
          • SIP does NOT carry voice, only signaling.
          • Voice/media is carried by RTP.
֎ Common SIP Messages:
          • REGISTER
          • INVITE
          • 100 Trying
          • 180 Ringing
          • 200 OK
          • ACK
          • BYE
          • CANCEL
          • UPDATE
          • PRACK
֎ Call setup :      INVITE →    =>   Voice media starts   =>   Call End
                        ← 100 TRYING              [RTP packets]              → BYE
                        ← 180 RINGING                                             ← 200 OK
                        ← 200 OK
                             ACK →
֎ Ports:
          • UDP 5060
          • TCP 5060
          • TLS 5061 (SIPS)

֎ In 5G (VoLTE / VoNR):
          • Used inside IMS only
          • SIP is not used for PDU session establishment. SIP becomes active only after IMS PDU session is established
          • UE ↔ gNB ↔ UPF ↔ IMS
          • RTP carries actual voice packets
֎ For VoLTE/VoNR:
          • UE sets up 2 PDU Sessions:
                      1) IMS APN/DNN → SIP signaling (default 5QI=5)
                      2) Internet APN/DNN → Data traffic
          • VoLTE/VoNR typically uses SIP & RTP over UDP.
֎ Encapsulation in 5G:
                    UE → UDP/TCP → IP → GTP-U → UPF → IMS
          • SIP is used b/w UE & IMS server through the 5G user plane.
֎ Without IMS PDU session → No SIP → No voice service.

pfcp.title: PFCP - Packet Forwarding Control Protocol
pfcp.content:
֎ Control protocol between SMF ↔ UPF.
֎ Layer: Application Layer (Control Plane Protocol)
֎ Transport: UDP (Port 8805)
֎ Between:
          • SMF ↔ UPF (N4 Interface)
          • Control Plane ↔ User Plane
֎ Purpose:
          • Tells UPF how to handle user-plane packets
֎ During PDU session, SMF sends PFCP messages to UPF to :
          • Creates GTP-U tunnels
          • Installs forwarding (PDRs) and QoS rules (QERs)
          • Create forwarding action rules (FARs)
          • Apply TEIDs
          • Manage session lifetime
֎ Main Rules Installed (Rules that tell the UPF how to treat UE packets) :
          • PDR (Packet Detection Rule)
          • FAR (Forwarding Action Rule)
          • QER (QoS Enforcement Rule)
          • URR (Usage Reporting Rule)
          • TEID allocation
֎ In PDU Session Establishment:
           1) UE requests PDU session
           2) AMF forwards it to SMF
           3) SMF selects UPF
           4) SMF sends PFCP Session Establishment Request to UPF
                         - PDR for Dl & UL
                         - FAR for forwading packets
                         - QER for QoS(5QI)
                         - TEID for GTP-U Tunnel
                         - Outer header creation (gNB IP + TEID)
           5) UPF installs rules & assigns TEIDs
           6) UPF sends PFCP Session Establishment Response to SMF
                  UPF confirms
                         - Rules installed
                         - TEIDs assigned
                         - Session ready
           7) SMF sends N2(NAS) message via AMF to gNB
           8) gNB uses TEIDs from UPF to build GTP-U Tunnels
           9) GTP-U tunnel becomes ready
           10) User-plane traffic starts flowing
֎ Heartbeat:
          • SMF & UPF exchange periodic heartbeats
          • PFCP Heartbeat Request/Response
          • If heartbeat fails → UPF considered down → SMF tears session
֎ Important:
          • PFCP is the brain controlling UPF
          • Without PFCP → UPF cannot forward UE traffic and PDU session would fail because UPF has no rules.
          • PFCP is control plane only (no user data carried).
          • PFCP is the last step before user data starts flowing.

gtpu.title: GTP-U : GPRS Tunneling Protocol - User plane
gtpu.content:
֎ This is the protocol that actually carries UE's data (Internet Packets) inside tunnels across 5G.
֎ User Plane Protocol
֎ Transport: UDP (Port 2152)
֎ Purpose:
          • Carries UE user data (Internet traffic)
          • Creates tunnels across 5G network
          • Encapsulates IP packets
֎ Between:
          • gNB ↔ UPF (N3 Interface)
֎ Encapsulation:
          UE IP Packet → GTP-U Header → UDP → IP → gNB → UPF
֎ TEID (Tunnel Endpoint Identifier):
          • Unique per PDU session
          • UPF assigns DL TEID
          • gNB assigns UL TEID
          • If TEID mismatch → No user data
֎ gNB & UPF IP address → Used as outer tunnel points
֎ Sequence numbers → Used for reordering in some vendors
֎ In PDU Session Establishment:
          • UE send PDU session request →
          • SMF selected →
          • SMF sends PFCP session establishment to UPF →
          • UPF creates TEIDs →
          • AMF sends N2 messages to gNB with TEIDs →
          • gNB builds GTP-U tunnel →
          • User-plane traffic starts
֎ GTP-U flow direction :
          UpLink : UE → gNB → GTP-U → UPF → DN         DownLink : DN ← UPF ← GTP-U ← gNB ← UE
֎ Features:
          • Each PDU session has at least one GTP-U tunnel.
          • All user data traffic (TCP, TLS, QUIC, SIP, RTP, DNS, anything) flow inside GTP-U
          • Supports QoS flows (5QI is mapped inside PDU session rules)
          • Supports mobility (handover reroutes tunnels)
          • Allows slicing (Different TEID paths for different slices)
          • Works with PFCP (PFCP installs rules; GTP-U carries data)
֎ Common Issues:
          • No internet even though PDU session established
                   - Wrong TEID
                   - Missing PFCP session
                   - GTP-U tunnel not created on gNB
                   - FAR misconfigured
          • UE works but DL doesnot
                   - Problem in DL TEID or FAR
          • High latency
                   - Problem in UPF CPU load
                   - Problem in GTP-U sequence numbers
֎ Without GTP-U → No user data flow

http2.title: HTTP/2 : Hypertext Transfer Protocol Version 2
http2.content:
֎ Upgraded version of HTTP/1.1
֎ Main signaling protocol b/w NFs in 5GC or Main application protocol used by the Service-Based Interface (SBI). ֎ Layer: Application Layer (Layer 7)
֎ Runs Over: TLS over TCP
֎ Improvement over HTTP/1.1:
          • Faster
          • Binary framing (not text-based like HTTP/1.1)
          • Multiplexing (multiple streams on one TCP + TLS connection)
          • Header compression (HPACK)
          • Server push
          • Can server many SBI messages at once
֎ Main Features:
          • Many requests on single TCP+TLS connection
          • Faster communication
          • Smaller headers
          • Stream IDs for parallel messages
֎ Used In:
          • Web browsers
          • APIs
          • 5G Core SBA (Service-Based Architecture) & SBI (Service-Based Interfaces)
֎ In 5G Core:
          • NF ↔ NF communicate using HTTP/2 over TLS over TCP
          • Runs over TLS 1.3 over TCP
          • Used between AMF, SMF, PCF, NRF, etc.
          • Heart of 5G-SBA signaling
֎ In PDU Session Establishment:
          • AMF receives UE request
          • SMF selection via NRF using HTTP/2
          • AMF talks to SMF via HTTP/2 to create PDU session
          • SMF talks to PCF for QoS rules & policy control via HTTP/2
          • PCF responds to SMF via HTTP/2
          • SMF accepts PDU session info & talk to AMF via HTTP/2
          • AMF responds to UE via NAS
          • All core control-plane decisions after AMF use HTTP/2
֎ Not Used For:
          • RAN signaling (uses NGAP over SCTP)
          • Direct user-plane traffic. APPs generally use QUIC(HTTP/3) or TLS over TCP(HTTPS) or Plain HTTP/2 over TCP.

rtp.title: RTP : Real-Time Transport Protocol
rtp.content:
֎ RTP is the protocol that carries actual voice/video media during a call.
֎ RTP travels inside GTP-U tunnel on user plane.
֎ Layer: Application Layer (Layer 7)
֎ Transport: UDP (Port not fixed → negotiated via SIP/SDP)
֎ Purpose:
          • Carries actual voice and video media
          • Used during active calls
֎ Used In:
          • VoLTE/VoNR/VoWiFi
          • IMS calls
          • Video conferencing
          • WebRTC
֎ Important:
          • SIP → Call setup (handles signaling)
          • RTP → Actual voice/media
          • RTCP → Quality feedback (jitter, loss, delay)
֎ In VoNR:
          • After SIP signaling completes:
          • UE ↔ IMS gateway exchange RTP voice packets
          • UE ↔ gNB ↔ UPF ↔ IMS ↔ RTP Server
          • RTP packets start flowing

֎ Encapsulation in 5G:
         (RTP over UDP over IP) → GTP-U → UPF → IMS

                 • SIP INVITES (contain SDP) : SDP specifies CoDec, RTP port, media diection
                                                      ↓
                                   • SIP 200 OK : Confirms RTP Parameters
                                                      ↓
                            • RTP Media starts : UE sends/receives RTP Packets
                                                      ↓
                             • Conversation happens : RTP flows continuously
                                                      ↓
                             • BYE, 200 OK : Call disconnect → RTP stops

֎ QoS:
          • Uses GBR QoS flow
          • Typically mapped to 5QI 1 or 2
          • Prioritized by gNB and UPF
֎ Quality Indicators:
          • Jitter (Variation in packet arrival time)
          • Packet loss (Missing sequence number)
          • Latency (Delay measured using timestamps)
          • MOS score (VoIP analysis tool that estimates call quality)
֎ RTP needs low latency + Jitter → RTP uses 5QI = 1 or 2 mapped to GBR QoS flow which is prioritised by UPF & gNB.
֎ Without RTP → No audio in call
֎ Works only when IMS PDU session is active (Internet APN doesnot carry RTP)

nas.title: NAS : Non-Access Stratum
nas.content:
֎ Signaling between UE ↔ AMF
֎ Type: 5G Control Plane Signaling
֎ Important:
          • NAS messages pass through gNB but gNB does NOT process NAS messages
          • gNB forwards NAS messages to AMF inside NGAP
          • NAS => Heart of UE ↔ Core communication
֎ Used For:
          • Registration
          • Authentication
          • Security setup
          • PDU Session Establishment
          • Mobility management
          • Deregistration
֎ Message Flow:
            UE ↔ gNB ↔ AMF
          • Outer Layer : NGAP
          • Inner Layer : NAS message
֎ Common NAS Messages:
          • Registration Request / Response
          • Authentication Request / Response
          • Security Mode Command / Complete
          • PDU Session Establishment Request / Accept
          • Deregistration Request
֎ During PDU Session Establishment:

                  • UE sends PDU Session Establishment Request over NAS to AMF
                    Includes:
                                    - DNN (APN)
                                    - S-NSSAI (Slice)
                                    - PDU Session Type (IPv4/IPv6)
                                    - SSC Mode
                                    - Requested QoS
                                                      ↓
                   • AMF forwards request to SMF through HTTP/2
                                                      ↓
                   • SMF creates session and send details to AMF
                                                      ↓
                   • AMF sends PDU Session Accept to UE over NAS
                     Includes:
                                     - Allocated UE IP
                                     - S-NSSAI (Slice)
                                    - QoS rules
                                    - Allowed session type
                                    - Security settings
                                                      ↓
                   • After this → GTP-U tunnel starts

֎ Security:
          • Integrity protected
          • Encrypted (after Security Mode Complete)
          • gNB cannot read or modify NAS contents
֎ Key Point:
          • All user-plane traffic starts only after NAS establishes the session
            • RRC  : B/W UE & gNB : Radio Control
            • NAS  : B/W UE & AMF : Registration, PDU Session, Security
            • NGAP : B/W gNB & AMF :Carries NAS messages + UE content management

          <----RRC (Radio Signaling)---->
          UE <----------------------> gNB <---------------------->AMF
          <------------------NAS (Core Signaling)------------------->

ngap.title: NGAP : Next Generation Application Protocol
ngap.content:
֎ NGAP is the signaling protocol between gNB & AMF
֎ NGAP = Transport layer for NAS + gNB specific procedures
֎ Type: Control Plane Signaling Protocol
֎ Between: gNB ↔ AMF (N2 Interface)
֎ Transport: SCTP (Port 38412)
֎ Purpose:
         • Signaling between gNB and AMF
         • Carries all NAS messages between gNB and AMF
         • Manages UE context in RAN
         • Supports handover signaling
         • Supports PDU session resource setup (Carries PDU session control info)

                        UE ----------> gNB ----------> AMF
                               RRC                      NGAP

֎ Important:
         • NAS messages are encapsulated inside NGAP
         • gNB cannot read NAS content
         • NGAP acts as transport layer for NAS
         • NGAP is the "Middle Layer" carrying NAS
         • Critical for creating GTP-U tunnels for user-plane
֎ Protocol Stack:
         • UE ↔ gNB → RRC
         • gNB ↔ AMF → NGAP
         • NAS carried inside NGAP
֎ Used During:
         • Registration procedures
         • PDU session establishment
         • UE context management
         • Handover procedures
֎ Role of NGAP in PDU Session Establishment:
                   • UE sends NAS : PDU Session Establishment Request
                                                      ↓
                   • gNB sends Uplink NAS Transport to AMF via NGAP
                                                      ↓
                   • AMF communicates with SMF over HTTP/2 and SMF creates PDU session
                                                      ↓
                   • SMF → AMF → gNB : Provides UPF tunnel information
                                                      ↓
                   • AMF sends PDU Session Resource Setup Request to gNB
                            Includes:
                            - UL/DL TEID
                            - UPF tunnel endpoint
                            - QoS rules
                            - QFI values
                                                      ↓
                   • gNB confirms GTP-U tunnel creation (PDU Session Resource Setup Response)
                                                      ↓
                   • PDU Session Resource Setup Response sent to AMF
                                                      ↓
                   • AMF sends NAS back to UE (PDU Session Establishment Accept)
                                                   ↓
                   • GTP-U tunnel becomes active and user-plane traffic starts

sctp.title: SCTP : Stream Control Transmission Protocol
sctp.content:
֎ SCTP is a transport layer protocol like TCP/UDP but designed for telecom signaling
֎ Layer: Transport Layer (Layer 4)
֎ Used For: Telecom signaling
֎ In 5G:
         • SCTP is used between gNB ↔ AMF
         • SCTP carries NGAP signaling (Registration signaling)
         • No user-plane traffic, no SBI traffic, no IMS traffic uses SCTP
֎ Protocol Stack:
                                                                                                                                                                                                        |                                                                         |
                            |       |                                                        |        |
                            |       |    |                                            |       |        |
    gNB     ==>     |       |    |      |           NAS              |    |       |        |            ==>     AMF
                            |       |    |              NGAP                     |      |        |
                            |      |                      SCTP                           |        |
                            |                               IP                                       |

֎ Transport:
         • SCTP over IP
         • Port: 38412 (NGAP)
֎ Main Features:
         • Multi-homing (multiple IPs/interfaces for high reliability)
         • Multi-streaming (parallel logical streams, no head-of-line blocking)
         • Message-oriented delivery (Good for signaling messages/ NGAP procedures)
         • Better control of association
         • Path failure detection
֎ Advantages over TCP:
         • Better for signaling traffic
         • Multiple streams avoid blocking
         • Supports redundant network paths
֎ Multi-homing feature can keep the NGAP session alive even if one interface fails
֎ Multi-streaming feature allows different NGAP procedures run in separate streams => no blocking
֎ Heartbeats are exchanged to check path health
֎ SCTP guarantees that NGAP messages must never be lost
֎ Used During:
         • UE registration
         • NAS transport messages
         • PDU session resource setup
         • Handover signaling
֎ Example Message Flow:
         UE ----(RRC)----> gNB ----(NAS inside NGAP over SCTP)----> AMF
֎ If SCTP Fails:
         • gNB loses connection with AMF
         • ALL UEs on that gNB deregisters
         • No new registration
         • No PDU session creation
         • No NAS transport
֎ SCTP is mandatory for 5G RAN ↔ 5G Core control-plane communication

rrc.title: RRC : Radio Resource Control
rrc.content:
֎ Signaling protocol between UE ↔ gNB
֎ Layer: Access Stratum (Radio Signaling)
֎ Purpose:
         • Establish radio connection
         • Manage radio resources
         • Security at radio level          • Handle mobility (handover)
         • Activate radio security
         • Carry NAS messages between UE ↔ gNB
֎ Scope:
         • Exists only between UE and gNB
         • Anything that go beyond gNB is NOT RRC, it becomes NGAP

          UE -----RRC carrying NAS----->gNB-----NGAP carrying NAS----->AMF

֎ Key Functions:
         • RRC Connection Setup/Setup complete (UE ↔ gNB)
         • RRC Configuration (PDU session establishment, Adding DRBs, QoS, Handover)
         • RRC Security Mode Command (gNB activates AS security)
         • RRC UL info transfer
         • RRC DL info transfer
         • RRC Measurement Reporting
         • Handover Control
         • RRC Release (UE goes back to Idle : Radio resource release)
֎ RRC Message Flow (Initial Access):
          1. UE → gNB : RRC Connection Request
          2. gNB → UE : RRC Connection Setup
          3. UE → gNB : RRC Connection Setup Complete
          This final message usually carries the NAS Registration Request.
          4. gNB → CORE : Forwards NAS inside NGAP
֎ Relationship with NAS:
         UE → RRC → gNB → NGAP → AMF
         NAS messages are transported inside RRC initially.
֎ Role in 5G Session Setup:
         • Moves UE from Idle → Connected
         • Setting security keys for radio
         • Passing NAS messages to AMF
         • Allocates radio resources for PDU session
         • Creates DRB (Data Radio Bearer) for user traffic
         • Enables GTP-U user plane later
֎ Important:
       Without RRC → No Registration → No PDU Session → No Internet
       RRC is the First protocol a UE speaks after it powers ON
       RRC is the transport layer for the first NAS message
       RRC sits at the bottom of signaling, closest to the radio
       Everything starts with RRc. Without RRC nothing can begin in 5G
       RRC packets can be captured only be decoded if you capture the packets in
         • UE modem
         • on gNB interface
       Normal PCAPs from UPF won't show RRC

bgp.title: BGP : Border Gateway Protocol
bgp.content:
֎ Layer: Application Layer
֎ Purpose:
         • BGP is the routing protocol that decides how data reaches other networks (Internet)
         • Exchanges routing information between large networks (Autonomous Systems)
         • It tells the UPF how to reach the internet
         • BGP is like Google maps for the internet(the world) & cars are packets
֎ Where it is used:
         • ISP backbone networks
         • Data center routers
         • Internet exchange points
         • Data Network (DN) side of 5G
֎ In 5G Architecture:

                    UE → gNB → AMF → UPF → DN Router → Internet
The DN router uses BGP to reach external services like Google, Netflix, etc.
֎ Important:
         • BGP is not part of 5G core signaling (like NAS / NGAP / PFCP...).
         • It works in the operator IP backbone network.
         • Critical after user-plane begins
֎ If BGP fails:
         • No internet routes available
         • UPF cannot reach external networks
         • UE shows "No Internet" even if PDU session exists
֎ Transport:
Runs over TCP port 179
֎ BGP exchanges:
         • AS numbers
         • Network (Routing) prefixes
         • Next-hop information
         • Best path routes
֎ Path Selection Factors:
         • AS Path
         • Local Preference
         • Next-hop reachability
         • Route origin
֎ BGP is not a part of PDU session signaling

diameter.title: DIAMETER
diameter.content:
֎ Layer: Application Layer
֎ Purpose:
         • AAA protocol: Authentication, Authorization, Accounting
         • Provides subscriber authentication and policy information
֎ Used In:
         • 4G EPC core
         • IMS network
         • VoLTE / VoNR voice services
֎ Important:
         • Diameter replaced the older RADIUS protocol.
         • It is not used inside 5G SBA core (5GC uses HTTP/2 + TLS for SBA functions).
֎ Where it works:
       IMS Core Components:
         • P-CSCF
         • I-CSCF
         • S-CSCF
         • HSS / UDM
           These nodes use Diameter to exchange subscriber information.
         • 5G Core NFs → use HTTP/2 + TLS
         • IMS Core functions → use SIP + DIAMETER + RTP
         • Data Session → use GTP-U + PFCF by PDU session
         • Policy/Charging → partially use DIAMETER when PCRF is used in EPC/IMS
֎ Transport:
Runs over TCP or SCTP
Port 3868
֎ Diameter Commands:
         • CER / CEA → Carrier Exchange
         • DWR / DWA → Device Watchdog
         • AAR / AAA → Authorization Request/Answer
         • MAR / MAA → Multimedia Authentication Request
         • SAR / SAA → Server Assignment
         • LIR / LIA → Location Information
         • STR / STA → Session Termination
         • UAR / UAA → User Authorisation
֎ Information Carried:
         • IMSI / subscriber identity
         • Public user identity (SIP URI)
         • Authentication vectors
         • QoS policy rules
         • Charging information
֎ Role in Voice Services:
      UE ---for IMS PDU Session---> SIP Register ------> DIAMETER to HSS/PCRF ------> Voice allowed
                IMS nodes use Diameter to retrieve subscriber profile and policy rules.
֎ If Diameter fails:
         • Subscriber authentication fails
         • IMS services fail
         • No VoLTE / VoNR voice calls
֎ DIAMETER is Not a part of PDU session establishment
֎ It directly affects : Voice QoS, RTP QoS, Charging used by IMS, IMS registration inside a dedicated PDU session

ospf.title: OSPF : Open Shortest Path First
ospf.content:
֎ Layer: Network Layer
֎ Purpose:
          • OSPF is an internal routing protocol used inside operator's IP networks
          • OSPF handles internal routing; BGP handles inter-domain routing.
          • Helps routers find the shortest path for packets
֎ Type:
Interior Gateway Protocol (IGP)
֎ Where it is used:
          • Telecom backbone networks
          • ISP internal networks
          • Data centers
          • Transport network behind UPF/AMF/SMF
֎ OSPF runs only between routers to -
          • Learn routes
          • Maintain dynamic topology
          • Build the shortest path
          • Auto recover from link failure
֎ Important:
          • OSPF is not used in 5G core signaling.
          • 5G core signaling uses :
                     - HTTP/2 + TLS + TCP, NAS, NGAP, PFCP, etc.
          • Transport n/w [The IP n/w connecting all nodes] uses :
                     - OSPF, IS-IS, BGP by routers that connect gNB ↔ UPF ↔ DN
֎ Transport:
          • Runs directly over IP
          • IP Protocol Number 89
                (Not TCP or UDP)
֎ What OSPF does:
          • Discovers neighboring routers
          • Exchanges link-state information
          • Maintains network topology map
          • Calculates shortest path routes
          • Automatically adapts to link failures
֎ Algorithm Used:
          • Dijkstra's Shortest Path Algorithm
֎ Routing Information Shared:
          • Link cost
          • Neighbor information
          • Network topology
֎ Relationship with BGP:
          • OSPF → used inside operator network
          • BGP → used between networks on the Internet

arp.title: ARP : Address Resolution Protocol
arp.content:
֎ Layer: Between Layer 2 and Layer 3
֎ Purpose:
          • ARP maps an IP address to MAC address inside a LAN in IPv4. IPv6 uses NDP instead of ARP.
          • Required before sending Ethernet frames
          • Without ARP → no packet can leave the local interface or UPF cannot forward any GTP-U traffic
֎ Where it is used:
          • gNB ↔ Router
          • UPF ↔ DN Router
          • AMF / SMF ↔ Transport routers
          • Any Ethernet-based link in the 5G transport network
֎ Important:
          • ARP is not a 5G signaling protocol.
          • It works below protocols like NAS, NGAP, PFCP, GTP-U.
          • ARP is not involved in PDU session signaling
֎ Example Flow:

                UE → gNB → UPF → DN Router → Internet

                     • UPF wants to send a packet to DN Router.
                     • UPF knows the router's IP but not its MAC.
                     • UPF does ARP Request:
                               "Who has 192.168.1.1 ? Tell 192.168.1.10"
                     • DN router ARP Reply:
                               "192.168.1.1 is at 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E"
                     • UPF now sends the packet using Ethernet.
֎ Important Behavior:
          • ARP Request → Broadcast
          • ARP Reply → Unicast
֎ If ARP fails:
          • Router MAC cannot be resolved
          • Packets cannot leave the local interface
          • UE may show "No Internet" even if PDU session exists
֎ Relationship with DNS:
          • DNS → Domain name → IP address, Global, Application layer, Uses servers
          • ARP → IP address → MAC address, LAN only, Layer 2/3, Mandatory for ethernet, uses broadcast

dhcp.title: DHCP : Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
dhcp.content:
֎ Layer : Application Layer
֎ Purpose :
          • Automatically assigns IP configuration to devices
          • Without DHCP, devices need manual IP configuration
֎ Provides :
          • IP address
          • Subnet mask / prefix
          • Default gateway
          • DNS server
֎ Transport :
       Runs over UDP
          • Server port 67
          • Client port 68
֎ DHCP Message Flow (DORA) :
          1. Discover → Client asks for IP
          2. Offer → Server offers an IP
          3. Request → Client requests that IP
          4. Acknowledge → Server confirms assignment
֎ Important :
          • In 5G networks, the UE usually does NOT use DHCP to get its IP.
          • UE IP address is allocated by SMF during PDU session establishment.
          • UE IP address is assigned by SMF and delivered via NAS signaling.
          • Delivered over : RRC → NGAP → NAS.
֎ Where DHCP is used in 5G :
          • Network infrastructure devices not UE
          • gNB nodes
          • Routers / switches
          • UPF / AMF / SMF management networks
          • Data center VMs or containers
֎ If DHCP fails :
          • Network nodes may not get IP addresses
                               ↓
          • Core nodes become unreachable
                               ↓
          • PFCP or GTP-U paths may fail
                               ↓
          • Therefore no internet
֎ After DHCP assigns IP :
          • Devices typically use ARP to discover the MAC address of the gateway.

ipsec.title: IPsec : Internet Protocol Security
ipsec.content:
֎ Layer : Network Layer Security
֎ Purpose :
          • Secures IP traffic by encryption and authentication
          • Provides VPN-like protection at the IP layer
֎ Protects data Against :
          • Eavesdropping
          • Packet tampering
          • IP spoofing
֎ Important :
          • IPsec is not a part of normal PDU session signaling.
          • But IPsec is very important to secure n/w interfaces & transport networks between nodes.
֎ In 5G Networks :
          • Commonly used between:
                  - gNB ↔ 5G Core over untrusted networks
                        IPsec tunnel protects NGAP + GTP-U traffic
                  - N2/N3 interface protection
                        N2 : gNB <--NGAP over SCTP--> AMF
                        N3 : gNB <-------GTP-U------> UPF
֎ 3GPP Security Options :
          • IPsec tunnels
          • Private MPLS networks
          • Physically secure transport links
If the network is not trusted, IPsec is mandatory.
          • Ipsec protects → NGAP(NAS), GTP-U
          • HTTP/2 + TLS protects → SBI
          • AS security protects → RRC/NAS
֎ IPsec Modes :
          • Tunnel Mode → Entire IP packet encrypted (new outer IP header added)
          • Transport Mode → Only payload encrypted
֎ IPsec Protocols :
          • ESP (Encapsulating Security Payload)
                   Encryption + Integrity (commonly used in 5G)
          • AH (Authentication Header)
                   Integrity only (rarely used)
֎ IKE (Internet Key Exchange) :
        • Used to negotiate:
            - Encryption algorithms
            - Security parameters
            - Session keys
        between peers before IPsec works.
֎ Important Note:
         • IPsec does not change protocol logic.
         • It only secures the transport path.
         • Without keys, packet captures cannot decode NGAP or GTP-U traffic inside the IPsec tunnel.

mpls.title: MPLS : Multi-Protocol Label Switching
mpls.content:
֎ Layer : Layer 2.5 (between Layer 2 and Layer 3)
֎ Purpose :
         • Fast packet forwarding technique used in operator backbone networks
         • MPLS uses labels instead of traditional IP routing lookups to carry traffic
֎ How MPLS works :
         1. First router attaches an MPLS label to the packet
         2. Core routers forward packets using the label
         3. Last router removes the label before delivery
Routers in the core do not inspect IP headers.
֎ Where MPLS is used :
         • Telecom backbone networks
         • ISP core networks
         • Data center transport networks
֎ Example path :
                   UE → gNB → MPLS backbone → AMF / UPF → DN Router → Internet
֎ Important :
         • MPLS is part of the transport/backbone network, not 5G Core signaling.
         • MPLS is also used between
                   - gNB ↔ AMF
                   - gNB ↔ UPF
                   - AMF ↔ SMF
                   - SMF ↔ UPF
          It simply carries protocols such as:
                   - NGAP
                   - PFCP
                   - GTP-U
                   - HTTP/2
                   - SIP / RTP
          But MPLS does not understand these protocols.
֎ MPLS Advantages :
         • Very fast packet forwarding (Label swap operation without full IP lookup.)
         • Traffic engineering
         • QoS guarantee
         • Network isolation (VPNs)
         • Predictable latency
֎ MPLS = Pre-defined fast paths through the operator's backbone
֎ Without MPLS : Every router checks IP destination & Runs routing logic
֎ With MPLS :
          - Edge router adds label
          - Core routers swap labels
          - Final router removes label
 Routers donot lookup at IP headers inbetween
     ֎ MPLS Label Contains :
         • Label value
         • EXP bits (QoS)
         • Bottom-of-stack flag
         • TTL
֎ MPLS is transport only, It is invisible to 5G logic
֎ MPLS vs Normal IP Routing vs IPsec :
         • MPLS → Fast forwarding, Private operator backbone, No encryption, Traffic engineering, QoS friendly
         • Normal routing → Every router checks destination IP
         • IPsec → Encryption & security, untrusted n/ws, strong encryption, confidentiality, security focused

                  - MPLS → in Private networks
                  - IPsec → in Public networks
֎ MPLS makes 5G transport networks fast, scalable, and low-latency
֎ MPLS Slicing :
         • Mapping slices → MPLS labels
         • Seperate LSPs for URLLS, eMBB, mMTC
         • Slice isolation at transport layer
